analysis.title: Americas Investment Banks: Key takeaways & updating estimates post earnings: FCN and PWP
key_insights: FCN reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $3.84 (reported EPS $2.35, adjusting for a $46.0mn special charge and $4.5mn litigation-related expense), 50% above GSe of $2.56 and 40% above Visible Alpha consensus of $2.74, on an adjusted EBITDA margin about 295bps above consensus with in-line total revenue.

FCN shares rose 14% on the day. GS attributes this to the 3Q beat and raised 2026E adjusted EPS guidance, a better margin profile after the headcount reduction, and negative investor sentiment going into the print on capital markets-adjacent names.
FCN raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $9.50-10.00 from $9.10-9.70. The midpoint is 5% above consensus. FY26 revenue guidance is unchanged at $3.94-4.10bn, which implies about 6% YoY growth.

FCN's 4Q26 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint implies a 26% miss vs. the Street and a 52% sequential decline (36% vs. $2.90 of 3Q26 core EPS per management). GS sees potential conservatism and forecasts the high end of the 2026 range.

FCN's 3Q strength was helped by no drag from Compass Lexecon, one-time benefits in Economic Consulting, record success fees at about 2x the normal run-rate, a favorable tax rate and favorable bad debt recoveries.

FCN announced a 4% headcount reduction with a $46mn 3Q special charge and a further $7mn charge guided for 4Q. The cuts target the Middle East and UK and businesses further from core strategy, such as the non-event driven Strat Comm business.
FCN management called the Restructuring market steady but was less constructive than investment bank peers, expecting subdued near-term demand while citing market share gains.
FCN expects the Economic Consulting recovery to take multiple years, with 3Q showing nascent signs. 4Q26 Economic Consulting adjusted EBITDA is guided near 2Q26 levels, about $1mn above the Street.

Slower regulatory enforcement remains a headwind for Forensic & Litigation Consulting, with several large engagements ending in 3Q. Management is positive on longer-term private credit investigations and AI-related regulatory matters.
FCN cut debt by $168mn QoQ after 6 quarters of debt growth and reduced capital return by 80% sequentially. GS expects buybacks to pause for the next 2 quarters.

GS raised FCN 2026E/27E/28E adjusted EPS by 7%/9%/5% on 30bps/30bps/10bps higher adjusted operating margin and a 2%/4%/4% lower share count, partly offset by lower segment revenue. FCN stays Neutral with a 12-month price target of $169 (from $151) at an unchanged 13.5x Q5-Q8 P/E.

PWP reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of 39 cents vs. GSe 18 cents and consensus 17 cents. Revenue of $251mn was 37% above consensus and up about 55% YoY, with a comp ratio about 3.0pp lower and non-comp expenses 5% lower than the Street.
PWP's 3Q revenue included a $55mn pull-forward from 4Q26. Excluding it, GS puts the revenue beat at about 10% vs. the Street. A large fee has also been delayed from 4Q26E to 1Q27E.

PWP leading indicators: announced and pending backlogs up 3x YoY, total booked plus announced and pending backlogs up 30% YoY, and gross backlog with engagement letters up 40% YoY. Management expects conversion over 1-2 quarters with minimal closing risk.

PWP is constructive on $1-5bn deals and strategic M&A, which is less rate-sensitive than sponsor deals. Management flagged highly leveraged private equity deals as exposed to rates and valuation disconnects. Energy M&A is recovering after a muted period tied to geopolitical tensions, and restructuring revenue is lower YoY on difficult 2025 comps.
PWP management reaffirmed a 2026E comp ratio of 67% (3Q26 62.5%, YTD 67%) and a single-digit % decline in 2026E non-comp dollars. Management said it did not initiate a sale process.
GS changed PWP 2026E/27E/28E EPS by -1%/+9%/+1%. It stays Sell with a price target cut to $14.00 from $15.50 as the Q5-Q8 P/E multiple falls 2.0x to 8.5x on lower market multiples.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised 12% from $151 on higher estimates after the cost plan and a rolled-forward Q5-Q8 window, at an unchanged 13.5x P/E. The 4Q26 guide implies a 26% miss vs. the Street.

Price target cut to $14.00 from $15.50 on a 2.0x lower target P/E of 8.5x reflecting lower market multiples, despite a strong 3Q beat and a robust backlog. Part of the beat was a pull-forward from 4Q26.

sector_views.rationale: Strategic and $1-5bn M&A is healthy and PWP's backlog is up sharply. Restructuring is steady to subdued, sponsor deals are rate-sensitive, and FCN is Neutral while PWP is Sell on valuation.

earnings_insights: FCN 3Q26 (reported 10/29): reported EPS $2.35, adjusted EPS $3.84 (excludes $46.0mn special charges and $4.5mn litigation-related expense), vs. GSe $2.56 and Visible Alpha consensus $2.74. Adjusted EBITDA margin 15.2%, about 295bps above consensus.
FCN FY26 guidance: adjusted EPS $9.50-10.00 (prior $9.10-9.70), excluding a $1.55 EPS impact from special charges and a $0.40 impact from litigation one-timers. Revenue $3.94-4.10bn unchanged.

FCN 4Q26 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint implies a 26% miss vs. consensus and a 52% sequential decline. GS 4Q26E adjusted EPS $2.13 (old $2.73), 2026E $9.94 (old $9.32), 2027E $11.54 (old $10.56), 2028E $12.59 (old $11.95).
PWP 3Q26 (reported): adjusted EPS $0.39 vs. GSe $0.18 and Visible Alpha consensus $0.17. Revenue $251mn, 37% above consensus. Comp ratio 62.5%, 3pp below consensus.
GS PWP estimates: 4Q26E EPS $0.25 (old $0.47), 2026E $1.63 (old $1.47), 2027E $1.50 (old $1.38), 2028E $1.75 (old $1.73). Figures as shown in the exhibit columns.
risk_factors: FCN downside: large-cap M&A and restructuring remaining weak while small-cap M&A accelerates and utilization falls across businesses.
FCN upside: restructuring accelerating significantly faster as small-cap M&A weakens, much larger share repurchases, or dramatically improved F&LC utilization.

PWP upside risk to the Sell rating: M&A accelerating faster than anticipated, with large-cap and strategic M&A continuing to outperform and generating growth and hiring without pressuring the comp ratio as much.
PWP: highly leveraged private equity transactions could be affected by the prevailing rate environment and valuation disconnects.
PWP: a large fee delayed from 4Q26E to 1Q27E and the $55mn pull-forward into 3Q create quarterly timing variability.
vol_and_positioning: Investor sentiment on FCN, as with other capital markets-adjacent names, was more negative heading into the print, which GS cites as a factor in the 14% stock rise on the day.
geopolitical: PWP's energy M&A activity was muted earlier in the year due to geopolitical tensions, with strong engagement and a solid pipeline now.
FCN's headcount cuts target geographies facing challenging market conditions, namely the Middle East and the UK.
cross_bank_references: FCN management were notably less constructive on Restructuring than many investment bank peers that have reported on the business.

tension_points.bull_case: 3Q adjusted EPS beat consensus by 40%, FY26 EPS guidance was raised, headcount cuts lift margins and management says Economic Consulting has turned the corner. GS raises 2026E-28E EPS by 7%/9%/5%.
tension_points.bear_case: 3Q was helped by one-time items (record success fees, favorable tax rate, bad debt recoveries) and 4Q guidance implies a 26% miss vs. the Street. Restructuring demand is subdued, regulatory enforcement is slow and the Economic Consulting recovery will take multiple years.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Large-cap M&A and restructuring remaining weak while small-cap M&A accelerates and utilization falls across businesses.

tension_points.bull_case: Revenue beat consensus by 37%, backlogs with engagement letters are up 40% YoY, announced and pending backlogs are up 3x YoY, and strategic and $1-5bn deal momentum is healthy with minimal closing risk.
tension_points.bear_case: About $55mn of 3Q revenue was pulled forward from 4Q26, a large fee slipped to 1Q27E, sponsor deals are rate-sensitive, restructuring revenue is down YoY, and GS cuts the target P/E to 8.5x for lower market multiples under a Sell rating.
tension_points.what_invalidates: M&A accelerating more quickly than anticipated, with large-cap and strategic M&A activity continuing to outperform and generating growth and hiring without pressuring the comp ratio as much.
